leads.name: Temple Newsam sweet chestnut 'thought to be 350 years old'
leads.reason: Only a Secret Leeds forum post (anonymous, same thread says oldest tree on Leeds council land until Oct 2002), no council, estate or register source, no coordinate. Yorkshire Gardens Trust letter says oak, lime, beech, sweet chestnut historically on the estate. Needs a Leeds Museums or council source and a pin. 2026-11-18 recheck: Flickr (tonygartshore, no geotag) says fenced beside the drive to Temple Newsam House; Geograph 259436 (Humphrey Bolton, 2006, CC BY-SA) shows a not-tall, enormous-girth chestnut at the end of the driveway to the stable block and home farm, subject precision only 100 m (53.7863,-1.459); not shown to be the same tree. Still no tree-level pin or official source.

leads.name: Roundhay Park veteran oaks and one ancient oak (Sept 2025 Yorkshire Gardens Trust tree-planting letter); a veteran oak 4.13 m girth at 1.5 m in the HDNS visit of 14 July 2020
leads.reason: Survivors of ancient field boundaries per YGT; no coordinate for any single tree, HDNS gives no location. No pin, no recognition line in reach.

leads.name: Harewood House champion trees (Japanese oak planted by Queen Alexandra 8 July 1908; Eucryphia, magnolia, London plane)
leads.reason: Harewood's own site says Yorkshire champion and perhaps British Isles champion, awaiting confirmation. Planted specimens, not ancient; paid estate; no coordinates; not 'Tree Register entry' seen. 8 miles north of Leeds city. Low priority.

leads.name: Shire Oak successor 'Son of Oak', Otley Road, Headingley
leads.reason: Held 2026-11-18: a replacement of about 1957 standing for the 1941-felled Shire Oak, so young; shipped only if a reader photographs it or the Leeds story is worth a young tree. OSM node 3615314054 at 53.81989,-1.57625 (approximate); alive evidence thin. Sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shire_Oak_(Headingley), headingleyleeds.com/explore-2/2017/3/23/the-original-oak
